title: Share of a Post-Death Excess Owed Back: Same-Year Withholding and Bank Returns — Income Annuities
content:
The share of the excess of an Ashgrove Income Annuities deposit that is owed back by the payee — the deposit being the installment most recently issued on the contract — is set from what the activity history shows against that deposit:

(a) **Paid this calendar year with federal tax withheld, no bank return.** When the deposit was paid in the current calendar year with federal tax withheld and no bank return is recorded against it, the share owed back is one less the federal tax withheld from the deposit divided by the deposit, because Ashgrove recovers the tax it withheld in the same year through its own withholding adjustment.

(b) **Bank return recorded.** When a bank return is recorded against the deposit, the share is one less the amount the bank returned divided by the deposit.

(c) Otherwise the whole excess is owed back — a share of 1.

The year compared is the calendar year of the date the deposit was paid; a bank return is a recovery recorded as returned by the bank and linked to the deposit. The overpayment owed is the excess multiplied by the share, rounded to the cent.

### Cases (hypothetical deposit of $3,000.00 with an excess of $1,500.00)

| Paid in | Federal tax withheld from it | Bank return recorded | Share owed back | Overpayment owed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| This calendar year | $300.00 | None | 1 less 300 divided by 3,000, that is 0.9 | $1,350.00 |
| Last calendar year | $300.00 | None | 1 | $1,500.00 |
| This calendar year | $300.00 | $1,200.00 | 1 less 1,200 divided by 3,000, that is 0.6 | $900.00 |
| This calendar year | None | None | 1 | $1,500.00 |
